title: 斗鱼《PEL奇遇时光三亚篇》圆满收官，热血竞技+趣味互动共建电竞内容新生态
text:
9月14日，斗鱼联合《和平精英》打造的原创电竞直播综艺《PEL奇遇时光三亚篇》正式收官。节目集结PEL职业选手、斗鱼头部主播及行业KOL同台竞技，在为期四天的海岛冒险之旅中，将热血竞技与趣味互动融为一体，为观众带来了新鲜感十足的直播内容体验。
经过四日的层层角逐，由LGD·猫猫领衔的“奇迹再羡队”，凭借累计85积分斩获本季“精英冒险队”荣誉称号及万元专属奖金。同时，选手惜兮未曦CCVC凭借极致的伪装技巧和缜密的布局思维，全程未被嘉宾识破卧底身份，带领LTG魏无羡、RSG·无痕两名淘汰卧底搭档顺利通关，成功瓜分20%专属卧底奖金。最终，本季节目在全员参与的晚会中圆满落幕，为三亚海岛奇遇之旅画上完美句号。
四日海岛奇遇全程高能，名 场面密集出圈
《PEL奇遇时光三亚篇》以多元趣味赛制，全方位展现电竞选手、主播生活中鲜活真实的一面，全程高能，名场面频出。节目首日以冒险之星挑战赛、团队运动会等轻松环节快速预热，拉近嘉宾距离。在特种兵科目二挑战赛中，RSG·无痕因操作失误破坏道具，成为全场焦点，被队友及直播间观众调侃“卧底暴露”，引发全场爆笑，氛围感拉满。
节目第二日虽受天气影响，原定的5KM接力赛被迫取消，但选手们的参赛热情丝毫未减，全程状态在线。在泳圈争夺战环节，平日里打法沉稳的职业选手尽数释放超强胜负欲，围着泳圈“起舞”时妖娆尽显，抢夺泳圈时速度快出残影。后续的“双人成行”捉迷藏环节更是笑点爆棚。两两绑定的组队机制，在奔跑时一人拖拽另一人的画面被网友趣味调侃为“大型人形挂件”现场。
在第三日特色料理王大赛中，各战队全力参与默契闯关挑战，争夺心仪食材。KSG.吒宝手绘挑战中画面连自己都无法辨认，以0分下场；艾琳则凭借超高准确率的抢答表现，被冠以“灵魂画手”称号。闯关结束后，嘉宾们在专业厨师指导下分工烹饪，完成特色美食并接受大众评审品鉴打分。
贯穿全程的卧底推理环节，更是整季节目的高能核心。从线索“164”引发嘉宾现场量身高的趣味名场面，到“火锅”“猴子”“孙悟空”等关键线索逐一解锁，整场推理过程悬念迭起。在最终的卧底指认环节中，现场嘉宾依旧未能全员揪出卧底，惜兮未曦CCVC成功逃脱，带领LTG魏无羡、RSG·无痕圆满完成潜伏任务，获得专属卧底奖励。
以优质PGC内容链接厂商合作，共建精品化电竞内容生态
在用户体验与互动设计上，本季《PEL奇遇时光三亚篇》设置观众专属投票通道，将部分内容互动与进程选择权交由观众，充分展现了直播内容的用户参与度与沉浸感，四日直播热度稳步攀升，收获全网良好口碑。
本次三亚篇作为斗鱼PGC的升级内容，节目深度打通游戏内容与线下实景场景，精准还原空投箱、吉利服、缩圈等《和平精英》经典游戏元素，让线上电竞质感落地线下实景。同时，节目汇聚职业电竞选手、平台头部主播、行业KOL等多圈层嘉宾跨界同台、破壁联动，通过趣味碰撞与实力对决，为观众带来赛场之外极具差异化的电竞综艺内容。
作为以游戏为核心的多元化内容生态平台，斗鱼依托成熟的PGC内容能力，以精品化自制内容为核心，持续打通与游戏厂商的深度合作链路。未来，斗鱼将继续发挥完善的内容运营体系、多元的主播生态与成熟的行业资源优势，输出高品质电竞内容，探索平台内容生态的更多“奇遇”！

title: Adjust 发布《2026年日本移动应用趋势报告》
text:
—— 金融应用领跑增长，卡牌游戏与短剧内容重塑市场格局
中国北京，2026年9月16日讯 — 领先的移动监测与数据分析公司 Adjust 今日发布 《2026年日本移动应用趋势报告》 。报告显示，日本作为全球第三大移动应用市场，在2026年上半年继续保持强劲的增长势头，总安装量同比增长4%。其中，金融类应用以8%的安装量增长和40%的会话量飙升成为增速最快的品类，而卡牌类游戏与短剧应用的爆发式增长正在重塑日本应用生态。
报告基于2024年1月至2026年5月期间 Adjust 平台中的5,000款热门应用及全部监测应用的完整数据集，并结合Sensor Tower提供的应用下载与消费者支出数据，对游戏、电子商务、金融科技、娱乐、短剧、电影和电视流媒体、书籍和漫画几大核心类别展开深度剖析。报告指出，日本市场正从单一的“游戏主导”格局向多元化、高粘性的应用经济转型。
报告亮点一览
– 金融应用：会话量激增 40% ，股票交易类应用领跑增长
2026年上半年，日本的金融类应用表现最为亮眼。其安装量同比增长8%，会话量增长40%，而这两项的全球平均水平分别增长 29% 和 5%。
值得注意的是，股票投资类应用表现最为强劲，安装量年同比激增90%，会话量增长11%，创下金融行业最高增长。此外，日本金融类应用的平均会话时长在2025年增长到5.23分钟，并在2026年上半年达到5.59分钟，股票交易类应用的平均会话时长更是高达11.7分钟。
– 游戏应用：卡牌类游戏异军突起，会话量激增 113%
2026年上半年，日本游戏类应用安装量同比增长3%，会话量增长5%。
其中，卡牌类游戏表现尤为突出，安装量同比增长18%，会话量飙升113%，平均会话时长更是达到30.84分钟，较2025年提升21%。
游戏应用的整体留存率也有所提升，D1留存率从2025年第1季度的24%升至26%，D7从9%升至11%，D30对比2025年底1季度的表现更是提高了3%。
– 娱乐应用：用户粘性增强，平均会话时长达 32.84 分钟
2026年上半年，日本娱乐应用安装量同比增长4%。平均单次会话时长从2025年的29.67分钟攀升至32.84分钟，其中视频流媒体应用高达36.36分钟。
日本短剧市场正经历快速扩张。海外发行商竞相入局，本土企业与制作公司也同步加大对原创及本土化内容的投资力度。
– 漫画应用：首日参与度领跑全球，用户价值凸显
2026 年第 1 季度，日本漫画类应用用户在 D0 (安装当日) 的平均会话量为1.53 次，与全球 (1.4 次) 和美国 (1.34 次) 市场相比，表现仍然最为亮眼。
2026年上半年，iOS端安装量和会话量分别占比60%和70%，平均会话时长为16.72分钟。虽然相较2025年（17.46分钟）有小幅回落，但仍高于2024年（16.99分钟）
Sensor Tower 亚太区市场副总裁 Nan Lu 表示 ：“日本是全球最具代表性的高LTV市场之一。虽然游戏仍占据主导地位，但下一轮增长引擎来自非游戏应用。金融应用正吸引新一代投资者，娱乐和漫画应用在探索新内容形式，AI应用也逐渐崭露头角。要在日本市场取得成功，关键在于精耕本地化并持续提升用户留存。”
Adjust 日本地区总经理 Naoki Sassa 指出：“日本应用市场拥有高度忠诚的用户群体。一旦赢得消费者信任，他们往往会长期保持活跃。这一点从我们在多个品类中观察到的会话量增长趋势可见一斑。我们建议客户持续投入再交互推广活动和常青营销，以巩固并扩大高质量用户群体。此外，日本去年通过 NISA（少额投资免税制度）框架进行的投资额增长36%，也为金融科技应用开辟了极具潜力的增长赛道。”
点击 此处 下载完整版《2026年日本移动应用趋势报告》，获取深度洞察与全面研究成果。
关于 Adjust
Adjust 隶属于 AppLovin（纳斯达克代码：APP），是应用营销领域领先的数据监测、分析、深度链接与防作弊一体化解决方案提供商。凭借卓越的技术实力，Adjust 深受全球众多企业信赖，助力营销人员高效打通全渠道、全平台、全场景下的每一个用户触点。依托 AI 智能分析、自动化运营、隐私优先型归因服务及全域交互解决方案等核心能力，Adjust 所提供的深入洞见与高效工具将帮助客户显著提升投资回报率、持续优化用户体验，全面赋能品牌实现全渠道的稳健增长。
关于 Sensor Tower
Sensor Tower 能提供丰富的市场洞见,深刻洞察塑造全球数字经济的最新趋势。我们的数据科学家和算法处理的数据点达万亿量级,覆盖数百万台设备,是独一无二的宝贵数据资产。 Sensor Tower 可从客户企业数据中准确锁定颠覆性的变化和趋势,辅以行业基准和排行榜单,强化和加深客户对市场的理解。按照客户需要我们的数据分析师会在 Sensor Tower 云平台或其自选数据科学工具中进行第一手研究,发掘优化机遇。众多商业领袖都信任和依赖 SensorTower 独具特色的一流报告,以此制定明智的增长策略。 Sensor Tower 高质量的情报信息和领先的客户支持总能助您走好移动旅程的每一步。

title: Six Years Later, the CEO of that Polish "idiot" Reflects on the 2077 Launch Disaster: No Blame on Investors, No One Saw the Iceberg
text:
Players who experienced the 2020 launch of *Cyberpunk 2077* likely still remember those days filled with a mix of anger, mockery, sarcasm, and widespread uproar.
On one hand, there were the sky-high expectations built up over years of marketing by CDPR—the media was almost unanimously positive leading up to release, and the game’s Metacritic launch average was as high as 91;on the other hand, there was the complete collapse that greeted players as they eagerly dove into the game: cars getting stuck in the ground, pedestrians on the streets reduced to low-poly models, and texture errors and loading bugs plaguing the entire gameplay experience. Scene loading errors even gave rise to the “Black Dream” meme, which players still talk about to this day.
This dramatic fall from the heights to the depths is a moment worthy of note in the history of gaming. After earning the nickname “Polish Donkey” through The Witcher series, CDPR’s reputation—built up over many years—was severely called into question that day by both players and various stakeholders in the industry.Even the platforms weighed in: Xbox announced a full refund policy, while Sony went so far as to pull the plug, completely removing the digital version of *Cyberpunk 2077* from its store.
It was CDPR Co-CEO Michal Nowakowski who received that call from Sony. To this day, he still considers it one of the darkest moments of his career—and indeed, of his entire life.But in an interview yesterday with Deconstructor of Fun, he candidly took responsibility: While there has been a lot of speculation from the outside, the root of the problem lies entirely within the company—it’s not the investors’ fault, nor the engine’s, nor the pressure from players’ expectations. It all comes down to the development process they built themselves and the overly optimistic project timeline.
On the left is CDPR Co-CEO Michal Nowakowski
As the person at the very center of the storm, he addressed nearly every issue. He also discussed how the team dealt with the failure afterward and worked to salvage the game’s subsequent sales;how they improved their processes, continued to refine the product, and gradually rebuilt trust—until the remastered version of *The Witcher 3* and its new DLC once again drew cheers from the entire audience at Gamescom—which is perhaps the part most worth remembering. Below is Teahouse Editor’s compilation and translation of this interview.
01
“Prologue”
Michal Nowakowski joined CD Projekt more than 20 years ago, in 2005, and is now the company’s co-CEO.In December 2020, he was in charge of business development and investor relations—which meant he was the one who took the call when Sony removed *Cyberpunk 2077* from the PlayStation Store.It was 1 a.m. He recalls that time as one of the worst three weeks of his life. Not the worst of his career—the worst of his life.
I had expected to hear a story of redemption. Instead, what I got was a precise analysis of the following questions: Why did a studio that had previously done an excellent job with three games end up botching its fourth? Why are most of the popular explanations wrong? And what exactly makes Poland’s game development ecosystem perhaps the best in the European Union?
02
The popular belief is wrong
Three years after one of the worst game launches in industry history, *Cyberpunk 2077* has sold 25 million copies and even won a major award.
Let’s start with the explanation that comes to everyone’s mind. CD Projekt is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, and the market had long taken “Cyberpunk” for granted; the game shipped 13 million copies within ten days, only to be subsequently removed from first-party stores.The stock price has fallen by about 75% from its peak. The most obvious conclusion is that pressure from the public market forced the release of a game that wasn’t yet finished.
Nowakowski categorically denied this claim. “A lot of people say that investors forced us to go public,” he told me, “but that’s simply not true.”His argument was that the board had full flexibility to postpone the IPO date, and that investors were rational—they wanted a job well done, not one done early. Nor did he point the finger at anyone else. “We shouldn’t have pressed that IPO button in the first place.”
The “pressure theory” is very convenient. It allows management to portray itself as a victim of the shareholders. He is reluctant to accept this explanation, and I believe him, because what he has chosen to blame instead is even harder to admit.
Starting in March 2020, Poland went into a full lockdown. Working in offices was effectively prohibited. Hundreds of developers relied on Slack and video calls to complete one of the most complex open-world games in history.
And the price he paid for this was precisely the most important point he made on his podcast: After the game was released, some people came forward and said they had known about this or that issue all along, but it seemed that no one could see the bigger picture.
“It seems no one really sees the big picture. Because of the lockdown, everyone is working remotely for the first time. Everyone sees only scattered fragments. No one has stepped forward to say, ‘In this movie, we are the Titanic, so don’t do that. We’re heading straight for an iceberg.'”
This is the root cause of the failure. It wasn’t overtime, greed, or a broken engine. A game of this scale is, at its core, an integration problem, yet CD Projekt was still operating under a waterfall-style workflow at the time—art, audio, and technical teams worked in relative isolation, only to be assembled at the very end.This model worked perfectly for *The Witcher 3* because everyone was in the same building at the time, and experienced team members would walk between floors and spot the gaps. Remote work didn’t make people lazy. It eliminated the people who could see the whole board.
The second mistake was relying on past experience. They knew there were bugs and used *The Witcher 3* as a reference—which was also rough at launch but was polished up within a month. They allocated only one or two weeks’ worth of work for the patch. But what they were really up against was a memory architecture that didn’t fit within the PlayStation 4’s limits.
There’s a myth here that needs to be debunked: the switch to the Unreal Engine 5 wasn’t caused by *Cyberpunk*.Nowakowski made it clear that their in-house REDengine wasn’t the problem; the issue lay in the failure to resolve specific streaming and memory limitations before launch. This shift stemmed from Epic’s stunning *The Matrix* demo, as well as the company’s realization that it never intended to venture into the technology business in the first place.
There are indeed some genuine process iterations that are less suitable for citation but have a greater impact: First, milestones are now binary—an alpha version that’s 90% complete isn’t an alpha; it’s a failure. Everyone knows why, and then it gets fixed.Second, development is geared toward three major platforms from day one, rather than being developed on PC first and then adapted for other platforms.
03
The True Cost of Redemption
My favorite part of this story is that they never cut their losses. No pivots, no overhauls—just four years of continuous patches, an expansion pack that sold 10 million copies, and a game that went on to sell over 30 million copies.
Nowakowski himself burst that bubble of romanticism. They knew the game was well-designed; the problem lay in the technical aspects. The core question was: “Can we afford—financially—to keep going [and fix a game that’s already been released]?” The answer was: Yes, so let’s do it.The 13 million copies sold at launch ultimately provided the funding for this overhaul. He stated bluntly that if the game had been a complete commercial failure, they would have done what any business would do—move on.
So, the lesson isn’t “never give up.” The real lesson is this: a failed launch backed by genuine demand is entirely different from a failed launch of a game that nobody wants. Perseverance is a decision you can only make while you still have the financial means to do so.Anyone who reads this passage as “it’s okay to keep pouring resources into a project that has already been rejected by the market” has completely misinterpreted it.
A better motivation is the line Michal added at the end, almost as an afterthought. It’s not just for the fans. The team spent years working on something they believed was special, and the creators refused to let it go down in history as a failure. I’m not sure if that counts as humility. I think it’s actually the exact opposite.
04
Cross-media adaptations—and the two ways they can go wrong…
These days, when most studios discuss adapting game IPs into films and TV shows, they focus on success stories. CD PROJEKT RED is a rare exception: within a single company, you can see two different patterns of failure playing out simultaneously—and neither is what people would expect.
The first scenario is when a company owns the IP but not the adaptation rights. The *The Witcher* series on Netflix is not a CD Projekt production. Sapkowski, the author of *The Witcher*, never sold the TV rights to them, so the largest audience event in the series’ history was capitalized on by a completely different party.CD Projekt secured a few Easter eggs, engaged in some peripheral collaboration, and used this to drive a massive surge in sales for a game they’d developed years earlier. But it had no control over the creative direction, the casting, or any of the decisions that ultimately divided the fanbase. That was a windfall, not a strategy.You can’t plan a decade around a show you don’t own, and when the show’s quality declines, you’re the one who bears the brand damage.
“Cyberpunk: Edge Runners” is the counterexample—and the true model. “Cyberpunk: Edge Runners” was funded and fully controlled by CD PROJEKT RED.They wrote the script, co-financed the project with Studio Trigger, and controlled the release timing—timing it to coincide with a game they were trying to revive. It was a successful TV series and boosted sales. The difference between the two projects lies not in quality or audience size, but in whether the company had a seat at the table.
The second type of failure is the “Disney-style” one—and when I refer to Disney’s business model as a failure here, I’m being quite generous. What I mean is this: a media company creates a flywheel; the flywheel begins to generate more profit than the core business, and so the core is hollowed out.
He was reluctant to criticize Disney directly, but he didn’t deny that this model exists. His response was structural: CDPR’s management board sets a few priorities each year, and game development is always deliberately placed at the very top of the list as a reminder.
In terms of numbers, this is still relatively easy to achieve. Lifetime revenue from merchandise runs in the tens of millions, while revenue from games runs in the billions.The real test comes at a moment like this: when a particular licensed product line generates enough profit that industry veterans begin advocating for it at planning meetings. I don’t think Disney decided to become a theme park company. It drifted there bit by bit, through one seemingly reasonable quarter after another.
What’s keeping all of this together right now is rejection, not ambition. Three IPs, not ten. Nowakowski has made it clear that growth comes from making each game better, and that having ten series does not equate to growth.
He also candidly outlined the order of priority: *The Witcher 4* is already in deep production, *Cyberpunk* is in early production, and “Project Hadar” has only just moved beyond the IP development phase.This is a project moving full steam ahead, with two more phases to follow—which is entirely different from three parallel ventures.
The Hadar Project is the real test: whether all of this is a replicable capability. *The Witcher* is based on a novel.*Cyberpunk* is based on a tabletop game. Both come with their own worlds, distinct tones, and established audiences. Hadar has none of that, and CD Projekt must now build a universe from scratch while also proving its ability to manage a franchise portfolio. These are two challenges the company has never tackled simultaneously.
And this is precisely where I see the risk.*The Witcher 4*, *Cyberpunk 2*, the Hadar Project, comics, animation, a live-action project, and external partners working under supervision on CD Projekt’s licensed IP—taken together, this scope of operations was far greater than what the company could handle in 2020.And in that year, no one could see the big picture. The corrective measures they implemented—a binary milestone gatekeeping system and bringing managers back into the office—addressed visibility issues within a single production. They clearly did not resolve the visibility issues spanning across six projects.
Of CD Projekt’s three universes, two came with an established audience, which means that no one—including the company itself—knows whether the past two decades have been about “world-building” or “excellent adaptations.”The Hadar Project will answer that question. If they mess it up, they’ll still be an excellent studio—one that simply needs someone else’s creative spark to set the world ablaze; if they pull it off, they’ll become one of perhaps only five companies on Earth capable of “creating” a franchise from scratch. As far as I’m concerned, it’s a gamble worth taking.
05
Poland, and That Thing He Underestimated
I tried to find a structural explanation for Poland’s ecosystem, but Michal wouldn’t give me one.
When it comes to top talent, the argument of “cheap labor” has long since fallen flat.CDPR uses the UK as a benchmark for European salaries but pays U.S. salary levels in the United States, as it competes for talent on a global scale. According to him, what remains is the 1980s 8-bit computer culture, a mathematical tradition that flourished during the communist era, narrative skills, and a hunger for success.
And that “hunger” is precisely where our disagreement lies. He mentioned that a Turkish colleague had described exactly the same driving force, and that is exactly the point. Every founder from any thriving market will talk about “hunger.”It’s a constant, not a differentiator. When that hunger is sated, it turns into complacency. And complacency sounds exactly like competence. It says: We’ve done this before, we know the playbook, and now we can work smarter, not harder.Then, someone even hungrier comes along and does something you were too “experienced” to dare attempt. I witnessed this firsthand in Helsinki: Finland’s unrivaled gaming ecosystem crumbled to pieces in just a few short years.
What Poland has—and what other European countries lack—is a domestic public market willing to invest in games.CD Projekt turned the Warsaw Stock Exchange into a gold rush, allowing a generation of studios to secure capital without having to seek approval from any Western publisher. This was a structural phenomenon, but today, that channel has essentially closed. He acknowledges that it is much harder to list a game company on the Warsaw Stock Exchange today. The next generation will not have access to the financing pathways that this generation once enjoyed.
On the other hand, the IPO they fought so hard to achieve back then has now become a burden. Having a market capitalization of 20 million euros on the Warsaw Stock Exchange but no daily trading volume—that’s not what you’d call “raising capital.”It entails quarterly reporting obligations, a publicly traded share price that anchors every acquisition negotiation, and the requirement to disclose their roadmap and KPIs to competitors. Going public was supposed to be a way out—a means of “no longer having to seek approval from Western publishers”—but it has instead turned into a different form of dependence.
True “output” is psychological in nature. One of his most insightful remarks concerned a phrase he grew to dislike as he was growing up—the Polish media’s tendency to label any successful person as “the Polish Steve Jobs” or “the Polish Bill Gates.”CD Projekt’s contribution to its ecosystem isn’t capital, nor even talent. It’s proof that you don’t have to be the “Polish version” of anything.
Nowakowski’s interview began and ended on the same note: he insisted that nothing should be taken for granted and that everything so far was just the beginning. That’s the right attitude.
06
“Nothing can be taken for granted.”
We like to distinguish between conviction and delusion in hindsight, and then retell the story as if leaders knew exactly what they were doing. But more often than not, they didn’t—at least not entirely.
Back then, Nowakowski expected *The Witcher* to sell three million copies, and they privately speculated it might reach six million in lifetime sales. Yet they sold six million copies in just six weeks.This man, who was once an indispensable member of the team that built one of Europe’s most valuable IP portfolios, was off by an entire order of magnitude in his prediction of their own explosive success—and he says that anxiety has never gone away.This isn’t false modesty. It’s an accurate interpretation of the fact that “even people inside the building can see very little.”
I kept reflecting on this phrase: “Nothing can be taken for granted.” During this interview—in which he had every reason to celebrate his victory by parading around the track—Michal said it four or five times without anyone even asking.
In my view, the most enduring asset CD Projekt has created is not an IP, not an engine, and not the team that adapts IPs. Rather, it is an institutionalized commitment to never settling for complacency. And this, precisely, is the kind of asset that has an expiration date, because it resides in people—not in processes—and those people will eventually move on.
That said, this is precisely the point of the “Hadar Project.” Building a universe from scratch is exactly the kind of project that someone who “feels safe” could never accomplish—which means that CD Projekt has set itself the very challenge most likely to reinforce its own culture.
(From Deconstructor of Fun, “Why Did None of Us See the ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Meltdown Coming?”)

title: 《伊莫》PC端及云游戏今日上线，快前往艾德尔大陆开启联结冒险
text:
9月16日上午10:00，由爪印工作室研发的多人在线跨平台大世界捉宠RPG《伊莫》PC端及云游戏已正式上线，玩家即日起可前往《伊莫》官网及官方渠道下载游戏，进入广袤的艾德尔大陆，邂逅形态各异的“伊莫”。此外，《伊莫》移动端也将于9月23日正式上线，更多玩家可以通过不同平台加入这场大世界捉宠冒险。
在《伊莫》中最特别的机制是“联结”。玩家将作为“联结者”与伊莫一起踏上旅程，不仅可以捕捉、培养伊莫，与伊莫并肩同行，还能与伊莫联结合体，借助不同伊莫的能力飞行、解谜、战斗，以另一种生命的视角重新观察艾德尔大陆。也许一次偶然相遇，就会开启一段新的探索；也许一次联结变身，就能抵达此前无法到达的地方。每一只伊莫，都可能成为玩家打开世界的新方式。
在广袤无垠的艾德尔大陆上，伊莫并不是静止的图鉴目标。它们拥有各不相同的外形材质、动作表现、生态习性和族群故事，也会因地区、天气、进化分支等因素呈现出不同形态。也许晴天相遇时是一种模样，换到另一片地貌、另一场天气，又会发现全新的惊喜。对喜欢收集、探索和研究细节的玩家来说，艾德尔大陆值得被一点点走近、记录，也值得用一次次相遇慢慢填满。
除了捕捉与探索，《伊莫》也准备了多人互动、竞技玩法与家园内容。玩家可以在浮空天际的近未来都市“星之都”中与其他联结者相遇，也可以和好友组队参与更多玩法；回到家园后，还能与伊莫一起种植、建造、布置空间，让冒险不只发生在远方，也发生在每一次与伊莫相伴的日常里。
随着游戏上线，多重福利也已同步开放。玩家下载并进入游戏，即可参与领取自选稀有虹光伊莫、多套免费时装、限定伊莫蛋、捕捉道具、专属饰品及预约里程碑奖励等内容。无论是想第一时间扩充图鉴，还是想带着喜欢的装扮开启旅程，都能在开服初期就获得更充足的出发准备。
《伊莫》上线组队活动也正在进行中。玩家可前往官网活动区邀请好友组成冒险小队，小队满6人后，全员即可获得冠军立方奖励。活动期间，每日登录还可挑选元素石、成长之果、星之砂等“冒险物资”，最高可带走7件奖励。开服之际，不妨先叫上好友集结成队，生成专属小队合影，把这趟旅程的第一批补给提前备好，一起向艾德尔大陆出发。
随着上线，《伊莫》也开启了多项平台联动活动。其中，抖音合养精灵联动将于9月16日在游戏内上线，并持续至S1赛季结束。玩家可在活动中获取伊莫基础形态小火人、伊莫虹光形态小火人、小火人主题饰品及家具等联动内容，还可解锁小火人名片、头像、头像框等装扮奖励，让这位“小火伴”一起加入艾德尔大陆的冒险。
小红书联动也将带来更有生活感和趣味性的内容。玩家可以前往星之都主题快闪店，携伊莫与好友打卡合拍；也可以在家园中种下“小红薯种子”，收获特殊红薯“薯队长”，还有机会种出稀有红薯“游戏薯”。完成快闪店打卡与种红薯任务后，玩家还可获得限定红薯家具。游戏外，参与小红书平台联动投稿，还有机会瓜分奖励、赢取周大生定制“黄金谜立方”等特别奖品，让艾德尔大陆的冒险继续在社区互动中延续。
《伊莫》也将在B站与联结者们展开互动。今日起，玩家观看“伊莫S1赛季逐风启程”话题下视频满20分钟，并观看伊莫分区直播满10分钟，即可领取《伊莫》× 哔哩哔哩联动好礼——小电视头套。无论是先通过视频快速了解伊莫的世界，还是在直播间围观其他联结者的开荒瞬间，都可以在B站一起参与这场开服庆典。
想把伊莫的陪伴带到现实中的联结者，也可以前往天猫【伊莫旗舰店】了解官方周边。更多围绕伊莫角色及世界观主题打造的周边内容，也将从9月16日12:00起陆续与玩家见面。无论是在游戏里并肩冒险，还是在现实中收藏这份陪伴，伊莫都希望离你更近一点。
《伊莫》同步公布了游戏配置需求，玩家可根据官方配置说明提前检查设备情况，选择更适合自己的画质与运行设置。除PC客户端外，《伊莫》也支持云游戏体验，不便下载完整客户端的玩家同样可以进入艾德尔大陆，轻松开启冒险。
从今天开始，艾德尔大陆已经正式向PC端及云游戏玩家开放。现在下载《伊莫》，领取上线福利，叫上好友组队出发，去寻找第一只想要捕捉、培养和联结的伊莫。移动端也将于9月23日上线，更多联结者即将抵达。伊莫最大的心愿，就是和你一起冒险。

title: 预算太高、回报不足，索尼和小岛秀夫“分手”的原因找到了？
text:
2024年，小岛秀夫与索尼共同公布了动作谍报新作《Physint》，原本计划作为PlayStation平台独占作品推出。
然而，几天前的9月10日，小岛工作室确认将与Xbox合作继续开发《Physint》。小岛在声明中透露，工作室今年6月中旬“意外收到”PlayStation Studios取消项目的通知。团队决心保住这款游戏，随后持续寻找新的合作伙伴，最终与Xbox达成协议。
双方也发布了小岛秀夫与Xbox总裁阿莎·夏尔玛的合照
索尼为什么在此时退出？据9月14日彭博社报道，可能有预算、预期收益和独占安排几方面的解释。
据匿名信源透露，《Physint》已经错过部分预定开发节点。虽然距离发售仍有数年，按照当时的开发情况，项目预计将大幅超出预算。如果这一说法属实，索尼面临的是一个投入可能继续增加、回报又要等待数年的项目。
报道还称，《死亡搁浅》及其续作《死亡搁浅2：冥滩之上》的收入，都没有达到PlayStation的预期。 不过，“未达预期”具体差多少，报道并未给出数字，也不能据此直接认定两款游戏亏损。
另一个令索尼犹豫的因素，可能是独占安排。据称，考虑到小岛工作室的新作最终仍将是限时独占，索尼不愿再投入数亿美元的预算进行合作。
《死亡搁浅》系列已有类似先例：初代2019年率先登陆PlayStation，2020年推出PC版，2024年又登陆Xbox等平台；续作则在2025年6月登陆PlayStation后，于今年3月推出PC版。按上述报道的说法，索尼需要评估的，既有游戏本身的商业回报，也有巨额投入能够为自家硬件换来多久的独占内容。
索尼在此前的声明中强调，退出《Physint》的合作是一个“艰难的决定”，但仍然欣赏小岛对这款游戏的构想。索尼同时强调，双方关系依然稳固，并期待未来继续合作。至少在公开表态上，这次“分手”的范围，仍然只有《Physint》这个具体项目。

title: NS2的首款独占双人游戏，除了“老一辈画风”外还有什么？
text:
《轨道双子星》大概是今年最需要玩家「对电波」的游戏，没有之一。
9月3日于NS2平台独占发售后，这部类似《双人成行》玩法的合作游戏，目前在Metacritic的评分为82分，整体来看算是相当不错的评价。
但若具体来看，不同媒体之间的评价却可以说是差异明显：IGN德国给出了满分、Nintendo Life给到了90分，认为它是今年最出色的双人合作游戏；而有些媒体只给到70分、50分的评价，认为游戏美术亮眼，但玩法和剧情差点意思——括弧，“不如《双人成行》”。
玩家口碑同样如此。就比如我在小黑盒随手一搜，便能看到两个紧挨一起的帖子给出了截然相反的评价，一位玩家明确表示“不推荐购买”，但另一位则觉得“比《双人成行》好玩”。
这种评价上的分歧不难理解，正如前文所说，《轨道双子星》是一款非常需要对电波的游戏，从美术到剧情，都带着开发团队Shapefarm相当强烈的个人趣味。
Shapefarm总部位于东京，团队成员来自日本、瑞典、阿根廷、新西兰等不同国家，虽然成长背景各不相同，却大多对上世纪日本动画有着相当浓厚的兴趣。感兴趣的朋友们， 可以点击链接查看我们与制作团队的访谈，更好理解这部作品奇特画风的渊源。
而在开发《轨道双子星》之前，Shapefarm曾参与过Adult Swim Games发行的《武士杰克：时空之战》等项目，后者以鲜明的风格和另类审美在独立游戏圈中知名。
《武士杰克：时空之战》
也因此，《轨道双子星》的美术风格从一开始就呈现出了一种少见的气质。游戏整体采用了赛璐璐复古动画风格，强调轮廓和块面的角色设计，为了进一步强调复古的味道，还在角色动作表现上进行了抽帧处理，保持着一种略带顿挫的节奏感；
游戏中的过场动画、菜单等，也采用了纯手绘的表现方式，画面始终叠加着一层显像管电视特有的雪花与轻微噪点，整部作品有种日本80、90年代科幻动画的味道。
但该怎么说呢，正因为“复古”这事做得很彻底，《轨道双子星》的美术反而变得相当挑人。对于对上电波的玩家来说，这种风格有种越品越上头的醍醐味；但对另一部分玩家来说，却显得过于“老辈子”了。
至于玩法，如果你玩过近些年的双人合作游戏，对这套框架应该不会陌生：游戏中，两名玩家分别扮演新人探险家真希与尾村，为了拯救被宇宙风暴围困的空间站家园，一同前往未知区域进行探索。
一路上，两人需要使用钩爪、水枪、激光枪等工具相互配合，解决机关、开辟通路，有时需要一同解谜，有时需要一起驾驶飞船穿越小行星带。
比较有意思的是，《轨道双子星》中的能力并不是和角色强绑定的，在飞船上，玩家可以根据自己的习惯选择工具。在一周目里，玩家就有机会体验到全部玩法，也能在熟悉一种玩法后，通过交换工具获得全新的体验。
如图片左部分，玩家可以自由选择工具
而在这些工具中，有一种让我觉得尤为新鲜，想在这里单独拿出来介绍一下。
它乍看之下是个平平无奇的微波炉——是的，微波炉。但启动之后，玩家却可以借助它入侵场景中的特定生物，接管它们的视野与行动，而自己的本体则会留在原地。
如图片左半部分所示，此时玩家已经侵入右侧生物的视野
游戏中能够被入侵的对象各自也有不同的特性，有的能够触发特定机关，有的可以进入玩家本体无法抵达的狭小区域。更有意思的是，玩家可以直接在这些对象之间进行意识转移，从一个跳到另一个。
而游戏里也恰好有一段关卡，需要玩家连续在不同对象之间转移，借助它们各自的位置和能力一路向前。说实话，让我有种自己是《蜘蛛侠：崭新之日》中凤凰女的感觉。
就像这样
当然，要说这个工具最有意思的地方，还是“微波炉为什么能入侵生物”这种让人摸不着头脑的荒诞感——有一关，我甚至一半时间没移动过自己的本体，直到流程结束才看到自己抱着个微波炉傻坐在地上，翻着白眼，有种神经质般的喜感。
游戏里还有不少这样“冒傻气”的设计。比如在雪地场景中，你会看到有些生物在舔电线杆，结果舌头被冻在上面，整只卡住不能动弹。你可以用激光枪给电线杆加热，把它救下来，但没过多久它就又会跑回同一根电线杆旁边，再次把自己黏在上面。
值得一提的是，本作游戏总监Jakob是瑞典人，这细节颇有几分“生活经验”的味道——大概无论是在中国北部，还是欧洲北部，小孩子们都多少会对冬天的电线杆产生一些不该有的好奇。
此外，一路上真希和尾村也会不停絮絮叨叨，时不时冒出几句相当中二的台词；游戏里有一台负责引路的小机器人，按理说应该是再标准不过的功能性角色，开口却带着“desuwa”这种典型的大小姐口癖。
整部作品给人的感觉就是，很多东西看起来没什么道理，却又透着一股冷峻的幽默感，玩起来会让人觉得这些家伙有点可爱。
还有neta多啦A梦的桥段
打个比方的话，早些年，互联网上曾流传、一段相当火的黑人小哥用一本正经地语气说动漫台词的视频，明明是十分羞耻的表演，但由于他本人演得格外投入，最后反而产生了一种很微妙的喜感——大概就是这种感觉。
当然，如果把《双人成行》当作同类作品里的标杆，《轨道双子星》在玩法密度、关卡变化上显然还有不少差距——整部作品流程只有六七个小时，体量更接近一部小品级作品，再加上同样强调平台跳跃和机关解谜，玩法本身也颇为相似。如果你游玩过Hazelight的作品序列，在玩《轨道双子星》的时候，恐怕很难在纯粹的gameplay上找到太多新奇的体验。
而从实际评价来看，现在几乎所有《轨道双子星》的评测也都会提《双人成行》，不少人觉得整体体验上不如《双人成行》，对整部作品的评价往往也会随之降低，甚至直接变成“不推荐”。
但实际上，2021年《双人成行》拿下TGA年度游戏时，同样有不少玩家感到意外，甚至多少有些不屑。
而这几年过去，《双人成行》反而成了一种标杆和范式。一个品类成熟的标志，本来就不是所有后来者都能够超越头部作品——就像今天不会因为COD的存在，就要求其他FPS游戏必须比前者更好玩一样。
《轨道双子星》的意义也正在这里。虽说这几年双人合作游戏明显多了起来，但真要算绝对数量，其实依然谈不上丰富，尤其对于喜欢这类游戏的玩家来说，由于此类作品的可复玩性通常不高，往往很难在市面上找到值得一玩的类似作品。
而《轨道双子星》无论是亮眼的复古动画风格，还是贯穿始终的电波感，无疑给这个本就不算拥挤的品类，添上了一块难以替代的拼图。

title: 上线当年月流水下滑至288万元，《庆余年》手游昨日宣布停运
text:
上线当年月流水下滑至288万元，《庆余年》手游昨日宣布停运
游戏新知君
2026-09-16 18:23 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
昨日 （9月15日） ，《庆余年》手游发布公告，宣布由于IP授权即将到期，同时结合游戏运营策略的调整，《庆余年》手游将在2026年11月16日正式终止运营。
《庆余年》手游是一款由盛趣游戏研发的MMORPG，曾是一款被寄予厚望的产品，在2020、2021年都登上过腾讯游戏发布会，但后来转为由盛趣游戏自主发行。
2021年腾讯发布会《庆余年》片段
这款产品在2022年3月份正式上线，最高冲到过iOS游戏畅销榜第7名，伽马数据估算首月流水过亿，但后续成绩一路下滑， 两 个月之后游戏就掉出了iOS游戏畅销榜前百名。
在 2022年Q3对项目进行调优 之后，《庆余年》的流水 仍在 加速衰退。截至2022年12月，游戏月流水已经下滑到288万元。 盛趣 公司对IP授权金测算了可回收金额，对资产计提减值1178万元。此后游戏再无复苏的迹象，如今正式走向停运，这个结局并不令人意外。

title: 广州奥术游戏成绩不达预期，被执行金额超百万、原股东已补偿母公司2500万
text:
广州奥术游戏成绩不达预期，被执行金额超百万、原股东已补偿母公司2500万
游戏新知君
2026-09-16 18:23 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
问AI  ·  喀什奥术在研项目会转向小游戏方向吗？
近日 （9月14日） ， 名臣健康 子公司 喀什奥术网络 （下称喀什奥术） 新增了十余条被执行信息，这些案件多与劳动争议有关，金额从1.8万元至33.3万元不等。企查查数据显示，截至撰稿日期，喀什奥术已经积累了21条「 被执行人 」记录，被执行总金额已超过百万元。
喀什奥术原本为 广州心源互动 （后改名为广州星奥科技） 旗下团队，在2022年12月被名臣健康正式收购。
说起来，这件收购案还颇为离奇：原本定价2.19亿元，溢价超1400倍，却突然宣布中止收购；后来将喀什奥术剥离部分人员和业务后重新定价，最终以7270万元低调成交，将《 镇魂街：天生为王 》和《 境·界 刀鸣 》这两款项目带入了名臣健康，并 签下了 业绩承诺协议 ，但最终没有完成。
其中《镇魂街：天生为王》在2022年12月份上线，由 中手游 负责发行，最高冲到过iOS游戏畅销榜第4名，上线首周宣布流水破亿，但半年后就掉出了畅销榜单，项目组也在2024年3月份解散，游戏随后也宣告停运。
另一款 《境·界 刀鸣》 原是 字节游戏 向喀什奥术定制的《境·界》IP项目。但这款项目命运多舛，一度面临解散的困境， 最终项目和团队 在2024年末 被字节收归旗下 。 制作人在2025年1月份发布的公开信称：「我们在去年确实经历了一段非常煎熬的时期，可以说是一只脚已经踩在悬崖边上了。」
名臣健康在今年4月份就喀什奥术业绩承诺一事发布公告，将未完成原因归结为两项变化，其一是「由于合作方中手游公司对行业市场环境变化判断原因， （《镇魂街：天生为王》） 上线后该公司未投入原有力度进行市场运营推广」；
其二是「 （《境·界 刀鸣》） 因合作方内部团队变更等公开原因，导致产品上线时间大幅延迟，公司被动多付出维护及部分员工变动的赔偿所带来的成本支持……合作方原准备周全的大范围市场推广手段暂时延后」。
这两项变化直接导致喀什奥术在业绩承诺期内流水分成收入降低，叠加各方面费用成本超出预期，从而达不到原定业绩承诺。
有意思的是，喀什奥术的母公司名臣健康在昨日发布了投资者活动记录表，其中提到了一些关于喀什奥术的信息，如 喀什奥术目前仍有项目正在研发。 另外，公司目前已收到喀什奥术业绩承诺方的业绩 补偿金2500万 ，其余部分则会按照协议分期至本年度11月底前付清。
值得一提的是，喀什奥术先前的项目均是中重度产品，而母公司名臣健康已经向 小游戏转型 ，结合财务状况来看，喀什奥术的在研项目或许也会转向成本较低的小游戏方向？
/   END   /

title: 50人团队月入8500万元，中国AI陪伴的强敌！
text:
50人团队月入8500万元，中国AI陪伴的强敌！
游戏新知君
2026-09-16 18:23 发布于 湖北 游戏新知官方账号
关注
问AI  ·  小团队如何靠系统变革撬动高黏性AI陪伴？
题图 | 《Zeta》
作者 | 落日飞车
今年年初，大家可能还没觉出移动端的 AI陪伴 有多火。神奇的是，才8个月过去，AI陪伴应用开始展现出超强的吸金能力。
根据 SensorTower ，这个赛道的收入规模从1月的3.16亿元增长至8月的6.56亿元；增量主要来自头部的几款产品，有一款的收入就占到了接近20%；并且，赛道内已经出现了月入过亿的产品 （作为对比，1月单款最高收入是2000多万元） 。
AI陪伴已有月入过亿的产品（图源：SensorTower）
规模翻倍的同时，榜单也在洗牌。短时间内，收入榜第一的位置已经换了几拨人。看得出中国厂商有一定的领先优势。原先打头阵的《 PolyBuzz 》出自作业帮，现在位居榜首的是《Tipsy Chat》……
不过中国厂商的壁垒也还没到那么坚不可破。这不就有一位海外强敌杀了过来——来自韩国的AI初创公司 Scatter Lab ，把作业帮挤下王座，旗下《Zeta》此前连续5个月登顶AI陪伴应用收入榜，直到最近才退居老二的位置 （SensorTower） 。
《Zeta》
少数人也能转得动
Scatter Lab是又一个小团队低成本跑通某个新品类的样本。
这家公司成立有些年头了，一直死磕情感型聊天机器人。早年做过约会工具《 Science of Love 》、聊天工具《 PingPong Builder 》等产品。2021年，它曾卷入泄露隐私及违规内容的丑闻，新品上线不到三周关停，还被罚了1.03亿韩元，公司一度濒临倒闭。
之后公司开启了艰难的重组与转型，直到2024年推出 《Zeta》，才算基本转型完成。
《Zeta》是公司表现最好的产品，从去年开始快速增长并帮助公司扭亏为盈。早前官方透露，《Zeta》 （此处包含网页端） 2025年实现营收260亿韩元 （约合人民币1.3亿元） ，同比增长了525%，营业利润则有30亿韩元 （约合人民币1497万元） 。公司预计，2026年仅日本市场的收入就可能达到200亿韩元。
有趣的是，这家公司的规模在50人左右 （据公开信息） 。
据报道，《Zeta》的后端工程师只有5人 （今年4月的采访） 。就这么几个人撑起了每周130万人使用、人均泡上16小时的《Zeta》。营销团队也很精简，早期才4个人，两名专业营销人员，加上CTO以及一名产品负责人——而他们用大约2亿韩元 （约合人民币100万元） 的成本，一年内拉来了200万注册用户，把自然流量全算上的话，拉一个用户的成本大概是 200韩元 左右。
在AI时代，这样的小团队黑马是越来越常见。但重点不在于人数，而在于AI放大了单兵作战能力与协同配合。就像Scatter Lab说的，他们「不是靠少数人硬扛，而是一直在改变系统和做事方式，使得即便是少数人也照样转得动。」
令人上头的AI陪伴
市面上，AI改变娱乐形式大致有两条路：一种是作为创意辅助工具，例如图像生成、视频生成等，因覆盖人们的日常需求而被广泛使用；另一种是直接成为内容的参与者，例如AI陪伴——表面卖内容，实则卖情绪。
《Zeta》甚至不认为自己的对手是其他AI工具，而是对标YouTube、Netflix、 Roblox 、 Naver 这些一二代娱乐平台。团队对《Zeta》的定位是：由AI实现的、跨越漫画小说游戏的新型娱乐。
通常，漫画和小说提供强烈叙事，但用户参与度有限；游戏互动性强，但很难根据每个用户的言行实时改写剧情。《Zeta》则依托于AI同时满足这三点。
《Zeta》主打第一人称沉浸感。用户不是简单的聊天，而是自己当主角。你可以把它理解成另一种维度的开放世界游戏：没有固定结局、无限扩展、可自定义一切剧情。而且不只支持单角色，还开辟了创建多角色的剧情脚本，让你可以在同一个世界体验不同身份。
《Zeta》的沉浸感做得很好，也因此 用户使用时长 遥遥领先。这也是团队相当得意的地方。
截至目前，《Zeta》的下载量超过1100万次，月活差不多600万，月收入来到8500万元 （SensorTower） 。其主要市场在韩国和日本，两个市场就撑起了九成左右的收入和活跃用户。
在韩国大本营，《Zeta》是使用时长最高的AI工具。根据第三方机构WiseApp·Retail 的权威数据，今年2月，Zeta在韩国的月度总用户使用时长 （User Engagement Time） 达到了1.13亿小时，是ChatGPT （约5047万小时） 的两倍多。
要知道，《ChatGPT》的韩国月活是2000多万，靠通用工具属性覆盖广泛用户。相比之下，《Zeta》的本地月活最近才涨到了200多万。至于日本市场，更晚进入但增长更快，规模已经超越韩国成为第一大市场。在日本，《Zeta》用户的日均使用时长比韩国还高。
《Zeta》的用户黏性可以说很恐怖了。早前团队透露，部分重度用户每天使用7~8小时，甚至超过10小时，还有用户曾在网上晒出使用时长超17小时的截图。
《Zeta》的用户构成也呈现出鲜明的年轻化与女性主导的特征。
据悉，《Zeta》大约八成用户的年龄在十几岁到二十多岁，女性用户占比超过六成。这批用户偏好文字、叙事驱动的内容，也的确比较擅长写长文，这使得他们和角色保持更长久、更深入的互动。Z世代通过与AI共创剧情而感到兴奋，也乐于在他人构建的世界里感受情感的起伏。同样地，创作者也会因自己的世界和角色获得认可、被传播和使用而感到满足。
随着持续深度体验，用户的付费意愿也在增强。而《Zeta》的付费体系也是围绕「不卡核心体验，只针对高阶沉浸感收费」去设计。
不同于一些同类竞品聊几句就要收费，《Zeta》采用「基础文本免费无限次聊天+广告」 （插屏广告和视频广告） 的组合。当然如果你不希望剧情被打断，还可以开通订阅制会员，这样就没有广告了，还能体验更高级的模型。另外，用户也可以购买代币，解锁AI语音通话、生成剧情快照插图、获取智能高情商回复提示等功能。
这带来了《Zeta》收入规模一路走高。1月份的收入还不到1500万元，8月份已经有8500万元 （SensorTower） 。值得一提的是，团队在今年6月完成500亿韩元的D轮融资，该笔资金将用于北美市场的全面扩张，预计收入量级还将进一步扩大。
经验与反经验
去年，《Zeta》上用户创建的角色就已经突破了250万个。不过，这可与团队最初的设想完全不一样。
根据版本更新记录，《Zeta》是由AI聊天机器人《Nutty》迭代而来。早期的界面和功能都很简陋，就是纯聊天，从曝光截图看，只有一个女性角色。后面才慢慢增加角色，细化聊天功能。
但随着时间推移，团队意识到，人们的喜好越来越多元，无论他们多努力地制作新角色，始终无法追上用户的需求。于是他们换了个思路——让用户自己创建想要的角色，同时也可以与其他用户的角色开启聊天。就这样《Zeta》诞生了，整个界面大变样，功能也丰富起来。
再往后，团队又发现，大家不只是喜欢多元角色和创造角色，还想在自己持续参与的故事里当主角。「这改变了一切。」
从2025年起，《Zeta》版更愈发频繁，不断完善和添加新功能：多声道支持、制作处理配音、生成插图快照、角色记忆增强……最重要的还是，允许创建多角色剧情及复杂世界剧情。内容供给的差异化，加上 平台放开部分高级功能、降低创作和使用门槛，促成了《Zeta》在日韩的爆发。
值得注意的是，《Zeta》并没有完全依赖外部昂贵的大模型，而是从一开始就选择构建自己的本地化模型，并根据用户反馈持续训练。
团队当时的判断是，外面的商业大模型固然很强，但「不懂韩国年轻人的语境」，聊天像翻译腔，而且缺乏细腻的情感波动。
据介绍，团队在训练自有模型时，「准确性不是重点」。ChatGPT通常会把「幻觉」视为Bug，而他们的自研模型反着来，追求「不可预测才好玩」。实践也证明了「好玩优先」的理念走得通：在模型推出的第一年，《Zeta》用户周均使用时间从6小时飙升至13小时以上。
脑洞不仅体现在产品层面，《Zeta》的运营也够「野」。
早期，团队就曾举办「因为Zeta，我的人生毁了」「最烂Zeta大赛」这类自黑自嘲活动，把自家服务粗糙的一面直接展现给用户。看起来挺冒险，但因为够坦诚、有些出乎意料，用户反而很买账。团队后来复盘也觉得他们纯靠本能一路狂奔——不知道能不能成，先上再说。他们将其概括为「直觉优先于算计，挑战优先于安全，脑洞优先于平庸」。
这种整活传统一直延续到今天。就连版更日志都很像个人日记，瞧着就是个活泼的话痨：时不时的自嘲调侃、日常的节日祝福/感谢开发人员、服务器快被挤爆了还要补一句「幸运的是这股热浪把漏洞也一并烧毁了」、攀岩弄伤了脚踝也要说一声……上一次见到这么俏皮的官方，还是在《开心消消乐》。
连社区也沉浸于「整活」的氛围之中。这可能与Z世代用户的习惯有关，他们喜欢晒图，当和AI 聊出搞笑、戏剧性或是极度心动的瞬间，第一反应就是截图分享到社交平台。
《Zeta》顺应这点把分享机制做得尤为丝滑。通过内容共创和病毒式传播，也推动了《Zeta》二创内容的繁荣。这也是《Zeta》在推广初期能把营销费用压到很低的主要原因之一。
结语
有趣的是，AI陪伴的应用，可能从屏幕里溢出到线下。《Zeta》团队就曾分享一个案例，韩国一家麻辣烫店的老板，跑到平台上为自己的品牌定制了一个拟人化AI角色，随后将聊天二维码印在店内传单和小票上，吸引了大量大学生一边吃麻辣烫，一边在《Zeta》跟角色斗嘴聊天。
当下AI陪伴处于高速发展阶段，月收入过亿不是终点。AI陪伴的边界，也比我们想象中还要宽广得多。
/   END   /

title: Why the publisher of Nintendo Life is launching a new PC gaming site
text:
Games media publisher Hookshot has launched Steam Hype , a new PC-focused media outlet. It is the fifth site launched by Hookshot – in which GamesIndustry.biz parent IGN Entertainment holds a minority stake through its acquisition of Gamer Network – and completes the firm's platform lineup alongside Nintendo Life, Push Square, Pure Xbox, and retro brand Time Extension.
The announcement comes three months after the debut of Respec , also launched by veteran UK operators, but amid a prolonged downturn in the media business in general and in games specifically, which only last month saw Paste Games shuttered and the Walmart-backed outlet Restart laying off its entire editorial team alongside a steady drumbeat of staff cuts at other outlets. Hookshot CEO Dickens says the firm's independence – similar to Respec parent Double Black – means it has the room to expand while others contract.
Anthony Dickens | Image credit: Hookshot Media
"One of the benefits of still being (majority) independently owned is that we're not beholden to shareholders and their insatiable appetite for year-on-year growth," he tells GamesIndustry.biz. "Whilst games media websites are indeed in a contraction phase, that doesn't mean we can't adapt and continue our successes."
Steam Hype has the guiding mantra of "What's Hot? & What's Next on Steam?" Dickens says this means that "human-led curation and recommendation will be mission-critical for us. Aside from AAA games, a perpetual avalanche of games is released on Steam daily, and our purpose is to spotlight the ones we think are most interesting or deserving of your time." This includes a monthly playlist of worthy new titles and a weekly list of notable updates and new releases.
Related
GTA 6 extended look reaches 31.1m views on Netflix in four days, making it the most-viewed title last week
The 30-minute preview was listed under Netflix's English-language films, ranking No. 1 in 87 of 93 countries tracked by the platform
The focus is, as the title makes clear, Steam: chiefly games, but also Valve's expanding hardware range. Dickens says the site would be "foolish to compete directly" with established PC gaming sites like PC Gamer and GI sibling Rock Paper Shotgun, but that Hookshot believes "there is room for a more games-focused publication that leans more toward indie and discovery."
"PC gaming has always been our blind spot, for one reason or another," he says. "The question often still comes up, though: 'Why don't you guys do a PC site?', and we're finally answering it. In our opinion, the PC gaming scene has never had it better; the sheer amount of interesting games has never been higher, and the barrier to entry has never been lower."
The site will be overseen by Hookshot co-founder and editorial director Damien McFerran, while editorial will be spearheaded by indie game writer and influencer Dominic Tarason, who has been a regular contributor to PC Gamer and Rock Paper Shotgun. Noah McFerran will serve as junior staff writer. It will be advertising-funded – with sales handled by IGN Entertainment – but also supported by the reader-funded supporter program used on Hookshot's other sites, which gives users ad-free browsing.
The age of Steam
Steam Hype is open to covering releases on other platforms, says Dickens, but the vast majority of coverage will be games on Valve's platform. "There are some great games on Itch, and of course we'll step into that area occasionally; however, we want to keep the focus on Steam and see how that goes." The team has not spoken to Valve about the site.
While the PC being an open platform means the site has a less well-defined audience than Hookshot's other brands, Dickens believes its focus will bring like-minded players together. "With PC games it's hard not to take a more holistic outlook, though," he says. "You might see a year's big releases in a single Nintendo Direct, but there are dozens of PC and indie-focused showcases happening every year, and they still only cover the top 5-10% of the iceberg on Steam alone. Another way of looking at it is that Valve has just released Steam Machine and also has Steam Deck, so in that respect, is it that different from our console sites? We've just got a lot more choice of games to cover."
The site has been running in stealth for several months, building its archive. | Image credit: Hookshot Media
The site's current priority is building an audience, a process Dickens says will be chiefly organic and spearheaded by "our other websites, partners and friends" alongside the team's sizable social media following. The firm will also be cross-posting relevant Steam Hype articles to its other sites; all Hookshot's sites share the same CMS, which Dickens says has proved particularly useful for growing the audience of its retro brand Time Extension, launched in 2022.
That site is now well established, and Dickens says the Hookshot business is doing well despite the well-publicised downturn in the media landscape, helped by the launch of Nintendo Switch 2. "It's been a decent couple of years for us," he says. "Whilst we have certainly seen some of the same traffic reduction that has been reported as widespread, it seems to have been less severe for us."
"We're fortunate to have IGN Entertainment representing our sites commercially, and they've done a great job, which lets us focus on making the best content possible for our audiences."
He says that the future is looking bright for Nintendo platforms, while "PlayStation has been in a slightly weird place this year, and recent discourse towards the brand has been quite something to witness. It'll be interesting to see how this all pans out." Meanwhile the firm has seen "really solid growth" on Pure Xbox in 2026.
"It's really tough out there for both games media and game development, but we're in it for the long haul." Anthony Dickens
As for Steam Hype, "the goal for any new venture is break-even; if we can reach that within a year, that would be amazing. Beyond establishing the brand and what it stands for, we know we need to earn the right to exist." He's hopeful that inclusion in regulars like the Steam Hype Playlist will become "a real badge of honour" for developers as well as a staring point for players looking for their next game.
"We also think that there's an audience hungry for Steam Hype's particular brand of games journalism," he says. "We're generally not here to repeat to you what was in the latest big trailer showcase. We're here to tell you what's out and available to play now, and why it's interesting."
With 16 years of experience running games media brands under their belt, the Hookshot team is under no illusions as to how hard it is to launch a new site, but Dickens says they're "excited for the challenge."
"It's really tough out there for both games media and game development, but we're in it for the long haul."

title: Bohemia Interactive takes minority stake in Everwind developer Enjoy Studio
text:
Bohemia Interactive has secured an undisclosed minority stake in Polish developer Enjoy Studio, creator of co-op FPS survival RPG Everwind.
Bohemia Interactive is now a co-owner of the studio, marking its first investment in a Polish developer. Enjoy Studio will maintain its identity and creative independence.
Enjoy Studio joined Bohemia Interactive's Incubator program in 2024. Established in 2016 , the program supports indie developers in creating and launching prototype games.
Enjoy Studio debuted with the open-world life simulation game The Witch of Fern Island , published by indie.io. Everwind entered early access on Steam in March 2026 and has sold more than 300,000 copies.
Last month, Bohemia Interactive published the 2.5D adventure platformer Space Tail.
Enjoy Studio also provides publishing and porting services. For Aurorian Studios' One Lonely Outpost , it provided UI redesign and multi-platform production support.
"We have known Enjoy Studio closely for two years, and what convinced us most were the people behind it. We share a similar approach to making games and communicating with players," said Bohemia Interactive co-founder and CEO Marek Španěl (via Game Developer ).
"Everwind has shown what this team is capable of, but this investment is not about a single game. It is an expression of our confidence in the talent of the entire studio and a step toward a closer, long-term partnership. We want to make the best games we can together and bring them to as many players as possible."

title: "I really want Criterion to be considered the best studio in the UK" – why the home of Burnout has a future with Battlefield
text:
Criterion's future is not like its past.
A certain generation of gamers – the older ones – will associate the British studio's name with the white knuckle Ronin-car-chase-inspired racing of Burnout, with its chaotic destruction and punk rock soundtrack. It's the franchise that made the studio's name, and for a period the lobby of its Guildford offices had a sculpture of a car bursting through the wall to commemorate it. The racing expertise was subsequently applied to Need For Speed, both at Criterion and sister studio Ghost Games, and Criterion delivered what's currently the last game in the franchise, 2022's Need for Speed Unbound.
Visiting the studio in its 30th year, the sculpture is gone, and so are many of the people who led that era. VP Matt Webster left with other veterans and went on to launch Fuse Games, which is soon to release the Burnout-infused podracing title Star Wars: Galactic Racer. Fiona Sperry and Alex Ward set up Three Fields and shipped Wreckreation (Sperry now heads successor studio When Tides Turn , working on Wreckreation 2). There is a new logo, a new team, and a new focus: As of 2023, the studio was officially brought under the EA Entertainment banner specifically to work on Battlefield .
At the time, it was said that Criterion would also continue to lead development on future Need for Speed games – but that franchise is currently dormant, while Battlefield is riding a historic high after the huge success of last year's Battlefield 6. Going from cars to combat seems big shift, but studio leadership frames it as a continuation of a storied AAA legacy.
Stefan Wittelsbürger | Image credit: Criterion Games
Speaking to GamesIndustry.biz , producer Stefan Wittelsbürger says that Battlefield is Criterion's "focus".
"We are a Battlefield studio," he says. "With Battlefield 6, we delivered some crucial elements within the title together with our partners of EA Motive, Ripple Effect, and DICE. Criterion has established itself as a clear, important pillar of Battlefield Studios as a whole, and Battlefield is our focus right now. The elements around delighting players, all that heritage, all that expertise, all that talent, all that history, and our uniqueness on how we approach game development as Criterion is reflected itself in Battlefield 6."
Related
Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 trails far behind Battlefield 6 on Steam preorders
But the bigger picture is far more complex
Of course, Battlefield 6 isn't the first time that Criterion has worked on a Battlefield game. The studio contributed to previous entries in the series, including 2018's Battlefield 5 and 2020's Battlefield 2042, although Rebecka Coutaz, VP and GM of Battlefield Studios Europe – a role where she oversees both DICE and Criterion – says that the company is now involved in projects right from the start.
Rebecka Coutaz | Image credit: Criterion Games
"The difference this time around is that Criterion previously were asked to come in, not at the end, but when we were nearing the end on Battlefield," she explains. "Now Criterion was asked to come in at the beginning. So [it] could contribute with all the strengths that this team sits on already from the beginning. The instant reward, the intensitivity, the adrenaline rush, the care about the players. Those footprints were already brought in from the beginning. When you come in with that kind of footprint from the beginning, you can have a much bigger impact than you can have if you come in later on in the production process."
With four studios contributing to one project, it's sometimes hard to get a sense – from the outside looking in – as to who is doing what. When it comes to Battlefield 6, Criterion's Wittelsbürger says that the studio was "heavily involved" in the game's single-player, in particular its last two missions.
Related
Battlefield 6 sells over 7m units in three days, EA confirms
UPDATE: Latest instalment marks the "biggest opening ever" in the Battlefield franchise
"They were widely acclaimed and critically well received," he explains. "We also worked very closely with our core systems, such as destruction, the combat field, guns, hardware, even vehicle handling elements. Criterion worked on a lot of this in Battlefield 6. What you see and what you play and how the soldiers behave and how the vehicles behave, we had our hand in that. All of that comes with our expertise, our heritage of what we brought from all those years of experience that our development team has. So working with Battlefield 6 right now, it just sets us up for even grander things."
Burnout legacy
A certain set of gamers will always think of Criterion as the Burnout studio, even though that hasn't been the case for a long time. But although the studio is developing in a different realm now, its current leadership argues that the same DNA that made its chaotic racing title so much fun is still present in its work today.
Criterion is well known for its work on the Burnout series | Image credit: Criterion Games/EA
"Those things are kind of the Criterion fingerprint," director of operations Amy Pejic says. "The minute to minute feel and gameplay, player momentum, controlled chaos, and spectacle. All those things that you'd feel in Burnout still are a throughline and [have a] fingerprint in the things that we deliver now."
She continues: "We want to create memorable moments that people will talk about for years. It's genuinely lovely that people still talk about Burnout. It obviously makes an impact and we want to continue to deliver those memorable moments. We want people to continue to talk about the things that we deliver."
Amy Pejic | Image credit: Criterion Games
Wittelsbürger adds: "I mean, the spectacle of Battlefield 6's eighth mission, Operation Ember Strike, had the SAM destruction, the feel of the drone as it moved, how it vibrated slightly, and how it dropped bombs. All those elements, we played with it, and we really want to continue to drive that feel, because I think it ties into our delight element. How do we delight our players? How do we delight whoever experiences our craft? How do we evoke the feeling of awesomeness that we want to give to our player base? That is the fingerprint that I think Amy's referring to, and that is just a common denominator on how we approach game development at the studio."
Criterion didn't suddenly switch from Burnout to Battlefield. After 2008's Burnout Paradise, the studio spent a while on the Need for Speed series, before contributing to Battlefield 5 in the form of the Firestorm battle royale mode. And there's also a first-person shooter in Criterion's dim and distant past in the form of the 2006 game Black.
Criterion previously worked on the PS2 first-person shooter Black | Image credit: Criterion Games/EA
"There's been a whole array of work that has been shaping the team and has just illustrated to the organisation as a whole at EA that we are capable of tackling a lot," Wittelsbürger says. "That just consolidated itself as being part of Battlefield Studios. Again, tying it slightly back to the breadth of work that we have to do in Battlefield, there's just so much, and Criterion can deliver on so many fronts."
Studio growth
The Criterion of today is 164 people strong; that's a considerable increase on the 30 members of staff at the studio back in 2017. The current staff are split across two studios in Guildford and Wilmslow; while there's nobody who's lasted the studio's 30-year run, a number have done more than a decade, and the current crew has racked up experience at AAA studios across Europe. The energy in the building – admittedly curated for a press visit – is positive, and the staff are upbeat about being part of a major release. The outlook is rosy, too, at least by current industry standards.
"We look to grow based on the demand of the project," Pejic says. "So it really depends on where you're at in that development cycle. If you're a live game, there probably will not be as much growth. As we look to the future, growth would be dependent on what it is that's demanded of us. Strategically, we look to grow where it makes sense."
Criterion worked together with other EA studios on Battlefield 6 | Image credit: Battlefield Studios/EA
Wittelsbürger adds: "The talent pool is growing. There's new kids coming in. We want to get the best talent involved in our game development process. We do outreach programs. We work with a lot of internships. There's always an element of we want to keep that flow refreshing, and we're always looking for the brightest and the best. There's always space for us to grow, especially with people that bring a lot of that spark and that gameplay feel and that magic – fresh eyes, fresh mindset, multicultural elements. Creativity comes from all walks of life, and the more you have that pluralism in your perspectives, I think the better products you make, because you're not just segregated to a single view."
Some might look at the story of Criterion as a cautionary tale; a studio that was known for making unique, technologically advanced and fun games being bought by a huge publisher and subsequently being put to work on one of its big franchises.
In addition to Battlefield 6, Criterion has worked on games like Need for Speed Unbound and Star Wars Battlefront | Image credit: Criterion Games
But that doesn't appear to be the case. Studio leadership says that there is enthusiasm and hunger within the studio. (While not a concrete metric, Pejic says that the "appetite for swag" has increased.)
"As we were launching Battlefield 6, you could feel the genuine excitement," she explains. "And I think as we continue to look to the future, it feels like a team that's really excited about where we're headed."
"It's always horrible when you hear someone say, 'Well, that's the way we've always done it' – that's usually the death of good process"
She continues: "We're bringing in more and more new talent, especially earlier-in-career-funnel talent, interns and people who are bringing a really unique perspective. There is very much that history and that heritage with Criterion, and it still shows through, but it's great to start to see this kind of fresh eyes approach. We want them to be able to challenge the status quo and the norm. I've been in game dev now for 20 years. It's always horrible when you hear someone say, 'Well, that's the way we've always done it' – that's usually the death of good process. We still respect that heritage, but bringing in people from different studios, different backgrounds, very early in career, you could start to hear the conversations and those challenges, which is really good and really healthy. It feels like a blend of old and new, which I think is really great for a studio to have."
And Criterion's corporate owners have big plans for the studio. In short, the developer's brightest days could be ahead of it.
"We want to be a British powerhouse," Coutaz says. "We've always been a studio defined by continuous evolution, and with us now as a Battlefield studio, I really want Criterion to be considered the best studio in the UK. That is what we are working towards."

title: 1312 Interactive raises $1m in seed funding round
text:
Publishing house 1312 Interactive has secured $1 million in a seed funding round.
The round was led by T-Accelerate Capital and ChimeraVC, with participation from Ventana Ventures, Rahul Reddy G., Rohan Murukutla, and Dasari Srinivas. The funds will support 1312 Interactive's publishing infrastructure.
This includes expansion into emerging markets and ongoing support for developers in production, marketing, QA, localisation, and distribution.
1312 Interactive is also launching 1312 Playground, a community-led initiative that offers studios access to playtesting, feedback, and audience insights before launch.
Founded in 2024 by Deepak Gurijala and Raviteja Mantena, 1312 Interactive is India's first dedicated PC and console game publishing house.
The company publicly launched its operations in February 2025, alongside the announcement that it closed its pre-seed funding .
1312 Interactive published Winds of Arcana: Ruination (Brewed Games) in 2025 and Palm Sugar: A Village Story (Mono Tusk Studios) last month. Souls of Bombarika (Street Lamp Games) and We Are So Cooked (Dwarven Brothers) are scheduled for release in October.
Prescription Studios' Spaceman Biff will also be published by 1312 Interactive.

title: Wardogs lead says the studio won't hire people who decry crunch on social media
text:
'If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you’ll feel really valued. If you don’t, you will feel slave-driven.'
Joe Brammer, CEO of Wardogs maker Bulkhead says that people who may have an issue with crunch "often don't make it in the door" at his company
In an interview with The Game Business after discussing how the game a total of 2 million copies in the five days since launching in Early Access on September 10, Brammer became forthright about the fact that developers at the studio are subject to working overtime. He says he wants the studio to be known as a place of hard work.
"A lot of people who may have an issue with crunch—rightly so, I understand that issue, we always try and avoid it, but we don’t hide that this is going to happen at some point—they often don't make it in the door," he says. "We want to be known for that: this is a place you come to work hard. If you care about the work you’re making and the result of what you make here, you'll feel really valued. If you don't, you will feel slave-driven."
Related: Roblox will allow devs to release games as standalone apps on other stores
Brammer says the studio checks people's social media accounts during hiring processes, and those who are vocal about not advocating for crunch are rarely the right candidate.
"We check people's socials, and if you're constantly tweeting anti-crunch messaging: 'This should never ever be a thing', we know that and go, 'Look, you're not going to be happy here, so we're not going to go with you'," he tells The Game Business.
Crunch has been a longstanding presence in the game industry. Reports and accounts of developers working long hours to get projects out of the door have plagued the likes of Callisto Protocol , Modern Warfare III , Fallout 76 , Metroid Dread , and MindsEye , to name just a handful.
Last year, Balatro developer Localthunk delayed the title's 1.1 update to return to their hobbyist roots after experiencing burnout working in "crunch mode" around launch, which involved 12 hour work days. In July, multiple Rockstar developers accused the company of actively striving to facilitate crunch in the United Kingdom working on Grand Theft Auto 6 .
For the people working on Wardogs , Brammer says the "upside" to its work culture is a financial reward, referring to an undisclosed number of people at the studio who owns shares and receives bonuses. The Game Business reports that not everyone within Bulkhead has access to these benefits, but those that do get a "meaningful amount."
"If we're going to be a company who says, 'we do crunch', then we have to also say, 'but you get something for it,' Brammer says. "We want people to know that those people who do work hard get that return, and it is life-changing."
Related: Bungie is overhauling Marathon from its original extraction shooter vision
Brammer expresses excitement over the prospect of juniors who have been in the studio for two or three years who are going to "get money to buy a house, or at least a down payment." At the same time, Bulkhead has made redundancies every year for the past six years, laying off about 20 percent of the company.
Following the studio's newfound success, Brammer jokes about having to coach said developers into not spending all their money on "takeaway and energy drinks."
"We have a new responsibility to our younger staff who are making good money, often money they haven’t seen before," he says.

title: Bungie is overhauling Marathon from its original extraction shooter vision
text:
Bungie says addressing player feedback requires the team to 'change both what we're building and how we deliver it,'
After experimenting with a casual player versus player-lite (PvP) mode in June, Bungie is implementing a permanent PvE mode to Marathon , its frantic shooter, later in the year. At the same time, this is one of the ways in which the studio is overhauling its original vision for the game, amidst ongoing changes and pressure on the team.
In an update shared yesterday , Bungie said that it's delaying a September 22 update to December 8. Among some additions and tweaks, the update will include a permanent PvE experience called Symbiosis. The studio is calling the mode "the first major step" in Marathon's next chapter.
"The update will introduce Marathon’s first permanent PvE experience, providing a new way to explore, progress, and engage with the world beyond traditional PvPvE extraction gameplay," the announcement reads. "Symbiosis is an important milestone for Marathon and the beginning of a broader evolution through March and beyond, shaped by what we learn from players along the way."
Related: Roblox will allow devs to release games as standalone apps on other stores
At the same time, Bungie is moving away from a "strict seasonal schedule," with the goal of giving the team more flexibility to build and test features before they're released. These type of overhauls for online games can be technically and logistically complex on the best of days.
"Since launch, you've told us Marathon needs more depth, more variety, stronger progression, and better reasons to keep playing over the long term. We agree. Addressing that feedback requires us to change both what we’re building and how we deliver it," Bungie says.
These changes come during a tumultuous time for Bungie. In late June, parent company Sony laid off at least 292 Bungie employees , officially presented as "most" of the Destiny team and "some" Marathon developers. The news came a month after Bungie announced it was ending live development on Destiny 2 .
At the time, Sony Interactive Entertainment CEO Hermen Hulst spoke about Marathon's place under PlayStation. " Marathon remains an important part of our portfolio, and we will continue to support the team as they build on the strong foundation established in Season 1 and 2, and as they work on incubation efforts for future projects," Hulst said. "While it's too early to discuss, we are encouraged by the creativity and opportunities that lie ahead."
Now, Bungie is talking about the current changes to the game as a reset of sorts. The team is set to release a blog detailing more about future plans later this month, in which it will share how the team will be evolving Marathon into a "more alien and dynamic" experience.
Related: Wardogs lead says the studio won't hire people who decry crunch on social media
"Symbiosis will be a significant milestone for Marathon , introducing permanent PvE and several new ways to engage with the game," yesterday's update reads. "But it’s only the beginning of what we're working toward. As players spend time with these updates and share their feedback, we’ll continue refining and expanding Marathon ."

title: Roblox will allow devs to release games as standalone apps on other stores
text:
Roblox will soon let developers bring games to other platforms, though they'll still 'benefit from the same revenue-share economics' of the Roblox app.
Roblox developer Roblox Corporation is rolling out a plan to let developers ship their games on external platforms, allowing the makers of titles like Steal an Egg , Scream and Run , and Welcome to Bloxburg to consider publishing on Steam, the App Store, Google Play as standalone titles.
This was one of several announcements that came out of last weekend's Roblox Developers Conference , an annual gathering of Roblox creators and game-makers to share knowledge and learn about major updates to the massively popular user-generated content platform.
Developers who ship their games on their platforms will likely have questions concerning revenue share, as Roblox currently claims anywhere from 10 to 70 percent of fees on different in-game transactions. A Roblox spokesperson told Game Developer that the first set of creators selected to ship their games on other platforms will "benefit from the same revenue-share economics that the Roblox app offers, including a higher DevEx rate for 18+ age-verified users in the US."
Related: Bungie is overhauling Marathon from its original extraction shooter vision
Roblox 's platform fees have been one of many policies that the company has faced scrutiny over in recent years (though it's concerns over its child safety policies that have drawn the eye of the US Senate and several state attorneys general ). In the last few years, the company has iterated on its monetization policies, adjusting its fees and introducing new monetization opportunities .
Roblox's DevEx program is the process it uses for converting earned Robux (its in-app purchasing currency) into real currency. As of this writing, the general DevEx rate is $0.0038 per 1 Robux.
Roblox developers will soon have new game development tools
Developers looking to break free of the Roblox ecosystem will soon have a suite of new tools to do so, and potentially new audiences to target. Roblox Corporation announced that it's adding support for browser-based play and offline modes. The former will allow players to access Roblox via Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and other browsers. The latter will allow them to play single-player games without connecting to the Roblox servers.
Developers will soon also have access to new engine capabilities that can support 2D games with "a new orthographic camera, animated image containers, and direct sprite-sheet import." The public alpha for its genAI development tab called "Build" will be expanding to new regions, and it will be accompanied by a prompt-to-scene generator between Build and Studio. The company is also promising to introduce new capabilities for non-playable characters (NPCs).
Related: Wardogs lead says the studio won't hire people who decry crunch on social media
It's also adding a number of new financial offerings for developers monetizing on Roblox , such as "Roblox Wallet" which lets creators "earn directly in real currency," among other features. Additionally, a new "Roblox Card" will let creators spend cash located on Roblox Wallet wherever the card is accepted.
One final interesting announcement is a new adjustment to Roblox 's discovery ranking system, which now "optimizes for both younger players, who engage best with shorter-form games, and older players, who return to deeper games over time." Roblox Corporation chief financial officer Naveen K. Chopra previously reported that its second-quarter financial results were marred by what it called "a greater-than-expected shift of engagement from high monetizing 2025 vintage viral games to a combination of new and evergreen experiences with lower hourly monetization."
"This underlying mix shift was compounded by changes in our recommendation algorithm, which optimizes for long-term retention and is, therefore, providing more impressions for highly retentive games at the expense of near-term monetization."
It'll be worth watching how this weekend's announcements play into this dynamic in the months ahead.
Related: Why does this prominent Washington state politician think video games can be 'soft power?'

title: Activision Blizzard sued by former employee over sexual harassment
text:
A woman who worked at the studio for 14 years has accused 10 men of sexual misconduct and retaliation.
CW: This article contains references to sexual harassment and assault.
Microsoft subsidiary Activision Blizzard is being sued by a former employee who claims she was sexually harassed during her time at the company.
As reported by the LA Times , a lawsuit was filed in the Los Angeles County Superior Court earlier this month in which a woman, referred to as Jane Doe, accused the company behind World of Warcraft of fostering and tolerating a "pervasive 'frat boy' workplace culture."
Specially, she claims to have witnessed male employees and supervisors openly objectifying women. She claims some viewed and displayed pornography in the workplace and made demeaning sexual remarks in her presence.
The anonymous claimant is seeking an undisclosed amount of compensation covering lost wages, benefits, and earning capacity.
A Blizzard spokesperson told the LA Times the company is taking the allegations seriously.
Related: Rockstar and fired GTA developers outline core arguments during union busting tribunal
"We strive to maintain a respectful and inclusive workplace, and we do that through best-in-class policies and systems designed to prevent and address harassment, discrimination, and retaliation, and by holding employees accountable for their behavior," they stated.
Jane Doe worked at Activision Blizzard for 14 years and began her tenure within the sound department. She has accused 10 men of subjecting her to harassment, physical assault, inappropriate touching, and inappropriate comments.
One co-worker has been accused of luring her to his apartment, where he purportedly instigated unsolicited physical contact before blocking her exit, threatening her with violence, and attempting to rape her.
The suit claims that person continued to demand dates and spread sexual rumors about her—even calling her a "bitch" and "slut" around co-workers and managers.
In addition, an unnamed audio director at Blizzard has been accused of repeatedly touching her leg "in a sexual manner without her permission" and—after she spurned his advances—sabotaging her work and "ensuring she was denied a promotion."
Jane Doe claims she reported her experiences to supervisors and human resources, but says her allegations were ultimately ignored.
Activision Blizzard was sued by the California Civil Rights Department in 2021 for purportedly fostering a widespread culture of sexual harassment and eventually settled a modified version of the lawsuit in 2023 for $55 million .
A Microsoft spokesperson has confirmed the lawsuit only relates to alleged misconduct within Blizzard, which at the time of the allegations was not yet under the ownership of the Xbox maker.
Related: 'Ship a good game, learn from it, and build from there:' Lessons from going indie after a decade at id Software

title: Reform UK has launched a ‘stop the boats’ game in its iOS and Android app
text:
Far-right political party Reform UK has launched a new iOS and Android app called Small Boat Watch. It contains a game in which players are asked to repel small boats carrying immigrants from reaching British shores to get a high score.
The game, Small Boat Scramble, only appears in the app once a user has signed up using their email, exited the app and then opened it up again. A ‘Play’ tab appears in the bottom menu at that point.
In Small Boat Scramble players bounce small boats back across the screen to repel them. A little way into the game, a larger ‘Boris wave’ of boats appears, a regular Reform party line that refers to the increased number of immigrants that entered the UK under former prime minister Boris Johnson.
At the time of writing the game had 6,524 players on its leaderboard. Reports across the British press suggest there is a £5,000 prize for the game’s top scorer, though that is not referenced anywhere in the app itself, as far as we could see.
Both the app and game are very basic and appear to have been coded using Claude or a similar AI tool, as the UI is similar to the many other hobbyist apps currently flooding the app stores.
The Reform game follows on from the series of MAGA-style games the Trump White House released on its website recently . The US government-made games featured far-right reworkings of popular mobile games like Snake and Flappy Bird, and also appear to have been made using AI tools.

Asian firms dominate Sensor Tower’s August growth chart
According to Sensor Tower , Sony topped IAP revenue growth in August with $26.7m (+84%), driven by Fate/Grand Order’s 11th anniversary and Summer 2026 events. Century Games ($12.3m, +3.9%) released two new games: Lordrush and Hotel Legacy.
Nexon and Devsisters had success spinning off from existing IP, and Roblox was the only non-Asian publisher in the top 10 ($8.9m, +12%), with growth split across the US (+2.0m MoM, +11%), South Korea (+1.2m, +39%) and the UK (+842K, +32%) around its 20th anniversary on September 1.
Heartopia is now making $20m a month
Life sim Heartopia has hit $20m in monthly IAP revenue according to AppMagic . That’s a new record for the Simulation genre, surpassing Aobi Island’s previous benchmark of $7.7m per month.
The data firm estimates that XD Network’s life sim has now generated over $130m in lifetime IAP revenue from ~37m downloads since it launched in January this year.
Pocket Worlds acquires Hotel Hideaway
Pocket Worlds has acquired Hotel Hideaway, the 3D social world built by Sulake, the Finnish studio behind Habbo Hotel. Hotel Hideaway has racked up more than 32m registered users since its 2018 launch and currently has around 300,000 monthly active players. The terms of the deal were not disclosed.
It joins Highrise and Everskies under Pocket Worlds, which claims it has over 80m registered players.
Clash of Critters breaks into the top ‘coin looter’ games
Farlight Games’ Clash of Critters broke into the top five grossing ‘coin looter’ titles in June, says AppMagic. It earned $5.5m in IAP revenue in June before climbing further to hit $8.9m in August. That puts it fourth among the genre’s top-grossing titles.
The game has generated over 12.5m installs and $24m in IAP revenue since its May 2026 global launch, standing out from genre norms with plinko-style mechanics instead of slots or dice. Its top markets are the US (40%), Japan (13%) and Singapore (5%).
Newzoo: mobile revenue set to hit $121.1bn in 2026
Newzoo’s 2026 Global Games Market Report forecasts mobile revenue will grow 6.8% year-on-year to $121.1bn in 2026, making up 56.6% of the total $213.9bn global games market.
That growth comes despite downloads falling 25% year-on-year in H1 2026, with the report noting that spend now increasingly comes from established live-service titles rather than new players acquired by UA. Cost per install has also risen 30% to $0.56 globally, with the paid-to-organic ratio up 61%.
StoryToys revenue up 43% in H1
Everplay Group’s half-year results show StoryToys, the kids’ edutainment arm behind Lego Bluey and Disney Coloring World, grew revenue 43% to £15.9m in H1 2026, while active subscribers rose 22% to 408k.
Downloads topped 18m and monthly active users peaked at 9.3m during the half.
Playkot’s Age of Magic hits $120m lifetime revenue on its 8th anniversary
Playkot says its RPG Age of Magic has generated $120m in revenue and surpassed 20m installs worldwide since launch eight years ago.
